validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independent of GEM/wiki. Two independent, verified, non-GEM sources both name this specific pipeline: (1) offshore-technology.com/GlobalData market-data profile (byline kgi-admin, 2023-04-18; verified 200, content present) states a 130 km, max-30in pipeline from Bay of Tripoli to Nuqat Al-Khams, operator Mellitah Oil & Gas, owners Eni/NOC, 'expected to commence operations in 2025.' (2) libyasummit.com (2023-12-14) -- the sheet's cited URL now 404s live, but the content survives at the Wayback Machine (http://web.archive.org/web/20240614053608/..., verified 200, content present) and explicitly states: 'the 130-km NC 41-Mellitah Gas project to commence from 2025 and owned by Eni and the NOC.' The two sources agree on length, start year, and ownership -- this is a real, corroborated project, not a hallucination or GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are consistent with both sources (an offshore-field-to-onshore-plant gas export line) and with how GEM classifies the sibling Mellitah-bound lines in this same roster (P6707, P6715, P6716, P7617 -- all recorded as transmission); no reclassification needed, though note neither source uses the word 'transmission' verbatim -- it's the conventional bucket for this class of line in the batch. DUPLICATE: research into the concession naming (NOC/libyaherald/rigzone coverage of a 2025-10 exploration restart) confirms 'NC-41' (also spelled 'MN 41') is the SAME concession now formally renamed 'Contract Area D' -- and that Structures A and E, the specific gas-field development GEM separately tracks as P6715 (E Structure-Mellitah Gas Pipeline), sit inside Block NC-41/Contract Area D. Combined with the identical 130 km length, near-identical diameter (30in here vs 32in for P6715), same construction status, and same last-updated date, this is a real duplicate-detection flag against P6715 -- see recommendation. Ruled out as duplicate of the OTHER Mellitah-bound Libya pipelines GEM tracks (outside this roster): the existing, operating 'Bahr Assalam-Mellitah gas pipeline' (~109 km, 10in, online since 2005) and 'Sabratha-Mellitah Condensate Pipeline' (~107 km, 10in, condensate not gas) are both clearly distinct assets (different diameter, different/older status, different commodity for the second one). ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp 50%, Owner2=Eni SpA 50% -- confirmed by offshore-technology ('Operator: Mellitah Oil & Gas; Owners: Eni and National Oil Corporation') and libyasummit ('owned by Eni and the NOC'); the sheet's existing mellitahog.ly ref (Arabic company page, already verified 200) is consistent, no change needed. StartState/Province='Bay of Tripoli' and EndPrefecture/District='Nuqat Al-Khams' confirmed exactly by offshore-technology ('Begins in Bay of Tripoli...terminates in Nuqat Al-Khams'). SPEC: Length=130 km confirmed by BOTH independent sources explicitly (offshore-technology: '130 kilometers'; libyasummit: 'the 130-km NC 41-Mellitah Gas project') -- tier high. Diameter=30in confirmed by offshore-technology only ('Maximum of 30 inches'); libyasummit gives no diameter, so this single value stays medium-tier support (existing ref already verified OK, no change proposed). Capacity is genuinely not stated in either source, nor in the broader Structures A&E project materials I checked (which give field/platform throughput, not this specific line's capacity) -- left blank rather than force a number. StartYear1=2025 confirmed by both sources ('expected to commence operations in 2025' / 'to commence from 2025').

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched for anything newer than the sheet's 2025-08-20 update. The newest dated, independent evidence is from June 2026: Eni's own press release (2026-06, announcing startup of the related Sabratha Compression Project) explicitly describes 'Structures A&E, whose execution is underway to develop two offshore gas fields' with no completion date given; a Rigzone article the same week (dated 2026-06-30) confirms the same -- 'Structures A&E...execution is underway' -- and separately notes production increases are currently being routed via the existing Mellitah-Misrata coastal pipeline, not this new line. Both independently confirm the project (of which this NC-41-Mellitah pipeline is the field-to-plant export leg) is still under construction, not yet operating, nearly a year after the sheet's original 2025 target start year. Status=construction is therefore still correct and current as of 2026-06 -- no status change warranted. This is NOT stale/dormant: the project has ongoing, dated activity (a related compression project just started up in the same complex in June 2026), so the dormancy rules don't apply. Caveat carried into the Start [ref] and Delay [ref] fills: the 2025 StartYear1 target has evidently slipped, but no source gives a specific revised year, so I'm not proposing a StartYear1 change -- just flagging that 2025 should be read as an unmet original target, not a confirmed operational date.

summary: P6708 NC 41-Mellitah Gas Pipeline: existence, length (130km), start year (2025), and Eni/NOC ownership all confirmed by 2 independent verified sources (offshore-technology.com + a Wayback snapshot of the dead-linked libyasummit.com); Status=construction reconfirmed by June 2026 Eni/Rigzone reporting that the broader Structures A&E project remains 'in execution.' Main finding: a likely duplicate/double-count against P6715 (E Structure-Mellitah Gas Pipeline) -- both are ~130km lines out of the same NC-41/Contract Area D concession, updated the same day -- flagged for manual cross-check/merge. Also repaired six dead current_ref instances (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start all shared the same 404'd libyasummit.com URL).
